correctness.rationale: The complete Pansiot–Brlek square-factor classification as presented in Brown et al. 2006 Theorem 4.1 and Lemma 4.2 gives exactly the two 2-adic cases for square suffixes. Even-endpoint 2-letter and 6-letter conditions are explicitly derived from t(2m)=t(m), t(2m+1)=1-t(m); odd endpoints desubstitute. Pair and fourgram recurrences are proved for all powers and yield \(A(2^r)=(2^r+9r-4-(r\bmod 2))/6\) for all r>=2. All-length halving counts give \(A(N)=N/6+O((1+\log N)^2)\). Direct independent full-square checks at 2048 endpoints, historical 32-term sequence, and dyadic formula for r=2..20 passed. Finite testing is not substituted for infinite proof.

evidence: Brown et al. (2006), Theorem 4.1 and Lemma 4.2, give complete square-factor forms and start-position alignment, so they justify the key desubstitution input but do not state a uniform cumulative count at all prefix ends.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general square-factor classification is used as an explicit premise, not presented as new. Translating starts of infinitely many scaled square families into end-indexed prefix counts, calculating their precise overlap, and deriving the parity-sensitive correction require additional recurrences. Power-avoidance theorems for other source words do not imply the count.

OEIS A093914 (2017 annotation) expressly calls density \(1/6\) an empirical suggestion; the present proof supplies an exact parity-sensitive count and controlled all-length error. value.rationale: The historical transform A093914 has a specific 2017 open-looking observation that its 1-frequency seems 1/6. The claim proves that motivated density along all N and the stronger exact all-r dyadic enumeration, with a parity-sensitive logarithmic correction. This is a natural word-combinatorial invariant, not an arbitrary finite statistic, and its exact law is nontrivial to recover from the published square classification.
